output.summary: Medium-sized deciduous tree native to the eastern and central United States and extreme southern Ontario, Canada. Its mature crown has upward-pointing upper branches, horizontal middle branches and drooping lower branches. Leaves are cut by extremely deep U-shaped gaps, with pale orange-brown tufts beneath at vein junctions; juvenile trees often retain dead leaves through winter.
output.edibilityNote: Acorns are described as very bitter and unpalatable unless traditionally processed; explicit human food use is not documented.
